explain.say: A camera sensor is a chip covered in millions of light-catching pixels. Each pixel is a photodiode: when light hits the silicon it knocks electrons free, and the brighter the light, the more charge builds up.

explain.say: A photodiode only measures brightness, not colour. So each pixel has a tiny red, green or blue filter on top, in a pattern called a Bayer filter, with twice as many green ones because our eyes are most sensitive to green.

explain.say: After the shot, the readout circuits measure every pixel's charge and turn it into a number. Software then fills in the two missing colours at each pixel from its neighbours, called demosaicing, to make a full-colour photo.

faq.q: How does a sensor turn light into electricity?
faq.a: Light is made of tiny packets of energy called photons. When a photon hits silicon in a photodiode, it can free an electron. The pixel collects these electrons during the exposure, and their number shows how bright that spot was.

It is a checkerboard of tiny colour filters over the pixels, in repeating groups of four: two green, one red and one blue. Each pixel records just one colour, and software combines neighbours to make full colour.
asks: How does a camera see colour?

faq.q: Why are there more green pixels?
faq.a: Human eyes are most sensitive to green light, and green carries most of the detail we notice in brightness. Giving green half the pixels makes photos look sharper and less noisy.
asks: Why does a Bayer filter have two greens?

faq.a: Each pixel has a tiny dome-shaped lens on top that bends incoming light into the light-sensitive part, instead of letting it fall on the wiring between pixels. This makes the sensor more sensitive in dim light.
asks: Why do camera sensors have lenses on every pixel?

faq.a: A megapixel is a million pixels. A 12 megapixel sensor has about 12 million light-catching pixels, though more megapixels only helps if the lens and light are good enough.

facts: Bryce Bayer of Eastman Kodak patented the Bayer colour filter pattern in 1976.
In a Bayer filter, half the pixels are green, a quarter red and a quarter blue.

quiz.say: A camera pixel sits under a red filter. What does it record?
quiz.show: A pixel under a red filter records…

options.show: How much red light reached it
options.say: How much red light reached it

options.show: Only whether it is day or night
options.say: Only whether it is day or night

quiz.why: The filter only lets red through, so the pixel measures the brightness of red light; software fills in green and blue from neighbours.

wrong.1: Each pixel records just one colour; full colour comes from combining neighbours.
wrong.2: It measures an exact amount of red light, not just day or night.
